guards.title: Escape in a first-level submenu returns to the menubar
guards.goal: Escape in the About submenu closes it and focuses About

attempts.failure: Model output truncated at max_tokens; reasoning may have consumed the output limit

plan.root_cause: The Escape key handler in submenus incorrectly calls `this.elements.rootMenu.blurChildren()`, which closes all top-level submenus (including the parent About submenu). It also uses `this.currentMenuItem.elements.toggle.close()` which is undefined for non-submenu items (like History), causing focus to move to the grandparent menu item (About) instead of the immediate parent trigger (Facts).
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the Escape key handler in the submenu's keyup listener to close only the current submenu's toggle (via `this.elements.toggle.close()`) and focus its trigger link (`this.elements.toggle.dom.link.focus()`), without blurring the root menu's children. This preserves the parent submenu's open state and moves focus to the correct parent menu item.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Escape in a first-level submenu (Facts) will now close only that submenu, keep the parent submenu (About) open, and move focus to the Facts trigger (#facts). This matches the APG keyboard pattern for submenus: Escape closes the submenu and returns focus to the parent menu item.
functional_risks: If the submenu's toggle reference (`this.elements.toggle`) is not set correctly, the close may fail. However, the initialization ensures each submenu has a toggle.
The change only affects submenu Escape handling; top-level menubar Escape behavior is unchanged (not defined in APG).
verification_requirements: Run the provided journey: seek #home, ArrowRight to #about, ArrowDown to #overview, ArrowDown to #facts, ArrowRight to #history, then Escape. Verify focus lands on #facts, aria-expanded of #facts becomes false, aria-expanded of #about remains true, and #history is not visible.
Test Escape in deeper submenus (if any) to ensure they close only one level.
